task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) for REQ-157: validate lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md and test/specs/REQ-157.md against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-157 acceptance_criteria and against the no-implementation-code constraint.

checks_performed.all_8_acceptance_criteria_mapped: PASS -- design section 7 maps all 8 REQ-157 acceptance_criteria one-to-one to concrete design elements (Capabilities grant_set/check/3, capability matrix + single fold, denial raise + host-readable value, service_capability parameterisation, now/fail ungated moduledoc statement, structural closed-set guard). No TBD/deferral language found anywhere in the mapped elements.
checks_performed.function_signatures_and_error_shapes: PASS -- Capabilities.new/0,1, add/2, has?/2, check/3, check!/3, service_capability/1 and Platform.install/1,2 are all given full @spec signatures with an explicit denial() error shape (function/required/granted). Capabilities.check/3's :ok | {:error, denial()} return is stated, not left implicit.
checks_performed.cross_module_dependencies_listed: PASS -- section 3 and section 8 give a full, correctly-directed dependency table (Platform -> Capabilities one-directional, Sandbox -> Platform unchanged call site, Platform -> deps/lua, Executor consumes transitively unchanged, forward references to REQ-158/159/160/162). Verified against actual source: sandbox.ex line 266 calls Platform.install/1 (arity 1) exactly as the design assumes, and executor.ex's rescue clause (lines 32-34) only calls Exception.message/1 on Lua.RuntimeException/Lua.CompilerException, confirming the design's claim that no change to executor.ex is required is correct.
checks_performed.denial_raising_mechanism_technical_verif: VERIFIED CORRECT, not merely plausible. Read deps/lua/lib/lua/runtime_exception.ex directly: the exception(list) when is_list(list) clause (lines 53-62) validates only :scope/:function/:message via Keyword.fetch!/2 but stores the ENTIRE keyword list unmodified as %Lua.RuntimeException{original: list}; message/1's list clause (lines 100-102) renders only those three keys. This means extra keys (:capability_required, :capabilities_granted) genuinely ride along unrendered on exception.original exactly as design section 6.1/6.2 claims -- a real, correct use of the library's own documented exception mechanism, confirmed by reading the dependency source rather than taking the design's word for it.
checks_performed.service_capability_parameterisation: VERIFIED CORRECT. Capabilities.has?/2 is specified as exact-string membership only (no prefix/wildcard matching), and the capability matrix's call_service row computes a fully-parameterised service:call:<svc_id> string per call from the first Lua argument. A grant of only "service:call:alpha" cannot satisfy a check for "service:call:beta" under exact-match semantics -- this genuinely prevents one service's grant from authorising another, per AC5. No gap found.
checks_performed.closed_set_pairs_enumeration_spike_dispo: ACCEPTABLE TO LEAVE AS OQ-3, not a blocking gap. Independently verified against deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/stdlib.ex (lua_pairs/2, lines 386-394) and deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/table.ex (Table.put/3, next_entry/2): table storage and pairs/next iteration are value-type-agnostic -- a function/native_func value stored via Lua.set!'s do_set_nested (deps/lua/lib/lua.ex lines 362-384) is stored identically to any other non-nil value and iterated the same way. pairs(platform) enumerating 8 function-valued entries is very likely to work as assumed; this is a low-risk, cheaply-verifiable assumption, and the design already names a concrete fallback (explicit introspection list or Lua.get!-based Elixir-side test) if it does not. Leaving this as a named, non-blocking spike with a stated fallback is acceptable and is not the kind of unresolved ambiguity this gate exists to catch.
checks_performed.no_implementation_code_present: FAIL. Per WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 1b(e) ('no actual .ex/.exs code blocks -- signatures and type shapes only, not bodies'), the design contains two full, working Elixir code blocks that are function/expression BODIES, not signatures or type shapes, despite being labelled 'illustrative': (1) section 4.4's install/2 fold body -- `Lua.set!(lua, [:platform, row.name], fn args -> Capabilities.check!(capabilities, row.name, row.required.(args)); row.stub.(args) end)` is a complete, syntactically valid anonymous-function body performing the actual gate-then-stub logic, not a type shape; (2) section 6.1's raise block -- a complete `raise Lua.RuntimeException, scope: ..., function: ..., message: ..., capability_required: ..., capabilities_granted: ...` expression is real, copy-paste-ready implementation code, not a signature. The accompanying disclaimers ('illustrative shape only,' 'no function bodies are specified by this design') do not change that the preceding text IS a function body in each case -- the disclaimer is self-contradicted by the content it follows. This is exactly the literal, no-partial-credit check WF-02 Step 1b(e) names, and per this role's own mandate ('FAIL immediately and completely on any single failed check -- no partial credit'; 'don't approve a design because it's close enough') this is not waivable because the rest of the design is otherwise strong.

issues: lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md section 4.4: the install/2 fold's illustrative Lua.set! call includes a full anonymous-function BODY (`fn args -> Capabilities.check!(...); row.stub.(args) end`), not a signature/type shape. Replace with a prose/table description of the required behavior (call check!/3 with the row's required-capability function applied to args, then invoke the row's stub on :ok) and, if a code-shaped illustration is wanted, limit it to the @spec/type level already given in section 2.4/4.1 -- do not show the composed closure body.

lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md section 6.1: the illustrative `raise Lua.RuntimeException, scope: ..., message: ..., capability_required: ..., capabilities_granted: ...` block is a complete, real raise expression, not a type shape. Replace with a description of the keyword-list shape (as already partially done via the denial() type in section 2.3) -- state which keys are passed (scope, function, message, capability_required, capabilities_granted) and their types/values without writing the raise statement itself.
